articles.body: 企业买 AI 系统，先搞清楚供应商是哪个流派——这决定了交付质量的天花板。 🔵 Palantir 流派：AI 是流程里被验收的工人 代表作 Palantir。核心思路： ▪️ 先把业务建成模型（本体/ontology）：资产、流程、规则、角色全部结构化 ▪️ 流程是确定性的管道，AI 只在被严格定义的环节里干活 ▪️ 每步产出可审计、可回滚、可复现 ▪️ 人始终在环路上（审核、放行、否决） 优点：结果可预测、可追责、错误可定位。缺点：前期建设重、慢。 🔴 AI Worker 流派：AI 是承包整个流程的承包商 代表作各种「AI 数字员工」「 autonomous agent」。核心思路：给 AI 一个目标 + 一套工具，让它自己规划、自己执行、自己纠错。 优点：上手快，演示惊艳。缺点： 不可复现 ——同样输入跑两遍结果可能不同；出错不知道错在哪一步；没法写进任何有合规要求的流程。 怎么选？看错误的代价。 ▪️ 错了就是客服话术不好笑一笑 → AI Worker 够用 ▪️ 错了是合规事故、资金损失、研究结论污染 → 只能 Palantir 流派 现实中的好系统是混合的 ：Palantir 的骨架（确定性流程、可审计）+ 在安全的环节里放 AI worker（自主检索、草拟、自查）。我自己做研究自动化系统就是这个架构：流程编排、验收门槛、数字溯源全部确定性，AI 只在「研究」「批评」这些被 gate 住的环节里干活——审稿环节有一票否决权，而且真的行使过（一次假设验证不达标，系统自己否决了自己，整个研究线标记 rejected）。 一句大白话总结： Palantir 把 AI 当员工管，AI Worker 把 AI 当老板供着。企业要的是前者。 本系列五课完结✅ 接下来上真实系统案例：六个行业的企业知识库，每个都能在线试玩，每篇都带评测数字。 AI #Palantir #…

articles.title: Why a Stop Hook JSON Error Came from printf %b
articles.excerpt: 📝 Originally published (in Japanese) at forge.workstyle.tech. TL;DR The Stop hook reported Unterminated string because printf with %b emitted a raw newline inside a JSON string. The hook also used a…
articles.body: 📝 Originally published (in Japanese) at forge.workstyle.tech . TL;DR The Stop hook reported Unterminated string because printf with %b emitted a raw newline inside a JSON string. The hook also used a cd path fixed to an earlier environment. Its change count missed staged and untracked files when it checked only git diff --name-only . TL;DR The Stop hook error Hook output looks like a JSON object but is not valid JSON — JSON Parse error: Unterminated string. occurred because the printf command’s %b format specifier emitted a raw newline inside a JSON string. I changed the hook to build JSON with Python’s json.dumps function, which converts values into JSON-formatted strings, and also reviewed where it runs and how Git changes are counted.

articles.title: I benchmarked 8 models on our own code reviews. The first bug was ours.
articles.excerpt: Claude Opus 5.5 failed the same review three runs out of three. Same pull request, same reviewer role, same result: the stage output "failed to parse", the review was marked errored, and Opus dropped…
articles.body: Claude Opus 5.5 failed the same review three runs out of three. Same pull request, same reviewer role, same result: the stage output "failed to parse", the review was marked errored, and Opus dropped to the bottom of my table. When I finally pulled the raw response, Opus had done exactly what it was asked. It wrote two short paragraphs explaining its findings and then gave a well-formed JSON object in a fenced code block. The problem was one phrase in the explanation: "the only production caller passes just { db } ." Our parser looked for the first { and the last } in the response and tried to parse whatever was between them. The first { belonged to { db } in the prose. So the slice started in the middle of a sentence, JSON.parse threw, and a correct review was thrown away.

articles.title: Right Now Is the Perfect Time to Play the Quietly Best Yakuza Spinoff
articles.excerpt: Like a Dragon Gaiden: The Man Who Erased His Name isn't a full-sized Yakuza adventure, but its compact scope makes the story hit especially hard
articles.body: When Like a Dragon Gaiden: The Man Who Erased His Name was released in 2023, the Yakuza series was in a strange position. The team at Sega's Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio was gearing up to give a heroic sendoff to longtime protagonist Kazuma Kiryu. They had big plans for 2024's Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth to pass the torch to a new main character. But Yakuza had unexpectedly become bigger than ever outside Japan, thanks largely to the viral success of Yakuza 0 throughout the late 2010s and early 2020s. The fans demanded more Kiryu, not less. And developer Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio rose to the occasion with The Man Who Erased His Name , an interquel that depicts his lonely years in exile after the events of Yakuza 6.

articles.body: TL;DR The Motorola Razr Fold (2026) is receiving a new security update after being stuck on the August 2026 security patch. Android 17 remains unavailable in the stable channel, even though cheaper Motorola phones have already received the update. Motorola has attributed the delay to additional foldable-specific optimizations, with no confirmed stable rollout date. For a phone that costs nearly $2,000, the Motorola Razr Fold has been getting some rather budget-friendly treatment in the software department. Owners have watched cheaper and older Motorola handsets move to Android 17 while their newer, premium foldable remains on Android 16. A fresh update is finally arriving, but it isn’t the one they’ve been waiting for.
articles.author: Hillary Keverenge

articles.title: 4-billion-year-old 'Rosetta Stone' found in Sahara Desert could unlock the secret history of water on Mars
articles.excerpt: A rock discovered in the Sahara Desert formed more than 4.1 billion years ago, making it one of the oldest Martian meteorites ever found. The ancient space rock offers a rare glimpse into the formatio…
articles.body: A rose-colored rock discovered in the Sahara Desert may hold some clues to Mars' ancient geological history. The meteorite , named Teghaza 001 after the salt plain in Mali where it was discovered in 2022, weighs roughly 1.8 pounds (800 grams) and formed more than 4.1 billion years ago. Blasted off Mars by an impact before eventually landing on Earth, it is one of the three oldest Martian meteorites ever found. The extraordinary age and unusual mineral composition of Teghaza 001 offer a rare glimpse into the formation of Mars' early crust and how volcanic materials may have been altered by water, according to a statement from NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California.

articles.body: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 6 – A… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. A Farewell to Swift Explanation: It is time to say goodbye to NASA ‘s Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory . After nearly 22 years of service, the satellite re-entered Earth’s atmosphere on November 4 at 7:39 EST over the North Sumatra region of Indonesia . The featured image is a mosaic created in 2018 using the first one million images captured by the satellite’s Ultraviolet/Optical Telescope .
